hitl_conditions: Operators remain decision-makers in processes needing judgment (in-plant logistics, on-site and remote supervision); the system informs, visualises and alerts but, by the authors' own limitation, does not yet integrate human behaviour into adaptive control.
key_finding: A three-layer DT architecture (Data, Knowledge, AI, 3D engines) with an industrial-process ontology was implemented in a lab factory and validated on in-plant AGV/crane transport: an LLM-RAG over a Neo4j knowledge graph answers operator queries in natural language, while knowledge-driven 3D safety zones alert crane operators; latency under 300 ms.

quotes.text: This work implemented the system framework in the Aalto Industrial Internet Campus (AIIC), which is a factory-scale lab containing autonomous robots, an overhead crane, and network infrastructures.
This paper presents a detailed implementation of the proposed system framework and validates it through a practical in-plant logistics transport use case.

In-plant logistics, distinct from fully automated systems, frequently require human intervention both on-site and for remote supervision. This study selects the in-plant logistics scenario as a testbed to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework.
The AI Engine incorporates ChatGPT-4 as its core AI model, with LangChain providing seamless connectivity to data sources within the Knowledge Engine's graph database.
To bridge this gap, we introduce a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) approach, which combines LLMs with external knowledge bases to improve their outputs.

while the proposed DT architecture emphasizes providing advanced interfaces and real-time insights to end users to facilitate informed decision-making, it falls short of fully integrating human behavior into the system for more adaptive control

Dudas: la IA solo recupera informacion (extension 1); la deteccion de colisiones es por reglas, no IA; testbed de laboratorio, no planta industrial. SCOR: Make.
